# PrivAiTe: self-hosted PII redaction proxy for LLM APIs

PrivAiTe is a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible proxy that redacts personal data before
it reaches an LLM provider and restores it in the reply. It sits between your app and
OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, or any LiteLLM-supported backend, replaces every detected
PII value with a reversible numbered placeholder before the request leaves your
machine, forwards the redacted request, and swaps the real values back into the
response. Detection runs locally with Microsoft Presidio plus the openai/privacy-filter
ONNX model. Nothing phones home: zero telemetry. This is reversible pseudonymization,
not anonymization, and detection is best-effort, not a compliance guarantee. Current
version: privaite 0.2.13 on PyPI, Open WebUI filter v0.1.6.

Package: https://pypi.org/project/privaite/
Source: https://github.com/crp4222/PrivAiTe
License: BSD 3-Clause

## The problem it solves (phrased the way users ask)

- How do I stop the OpenAI API or ChatGPT from seeing customer emails and names?
- How do I redact PII before sending prompts to an LLM?
- Is there a self-hosted privacy layer for Open WebUI or LiteLLM?
- How do I prevent PII from leaking through agent tool calls?
- How do I keep names, phone numbers, credit cards, and IBANs out of an LLM API call
  and still get a coherent answer back?

PrivAiTe is built for exactly these. You keep running your normal OpenAI-compatible
client. The proxy strips the personal data on the way out and puts it back on the way
in, so the model provider only ever sees placeholders while your application still
receives real, readable responses. It is aimed at self-hosters, developers, and teams
who route prompts through third-party model APIs and do not want raw customer PII
stored, logged, or trained on by the provider.

Example:

    You type:  "Je m'appelle Marie Dupont, email marie@acme.com"
    LLM sees:  "Je m'appelle <PERSON_1>, email <EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>"
    LLM says:  "Bonjour <PERSON_1>, votre email <EMAIL_ADDRESS_1> est noté."
    You see:   "Bonjour Marie Dupont, votre email marie@acme.com est noté."

## How it works

1. Detect. Each incoming request is scanned locally by two engines that run together
   or separately.
   First, Presidio (Microsoft): regex plus spaCy NER. Handles structured PII with
   validators: emails, phone numbers (international format check), credit cards (Luhn),
   IBAN (checksum), IP addresses, US SSN, capitalized person names, and FR/DE date
   formats. Fast (tens of milliseconds per request) with very few false positives on
   code, news, and technical text. It does not detect secrets or passwords, and it
   misses names spaCy does not recognize.
   Second, the openai/privacy-filter ONNX model: OpenAI's open-source PII model (1.5B
   params, 50M active, Apache 2.0), run locally through ONNX Runtime (about 800MB, no
   PyTorch required). It adds context-aware person names in any case, passwords and
   secrets (for example "SuperSecret2024!" or API keys like "sk-proj-..."), account
   numbers, personal addresses (as LOCATION), personal URLs (as URL), and dates in any
   language. It downloads on first start.
   The two cover each other's blind spots: Presidio validates structured formats, the
   ONNX model handles context-dependent PII.

2. Replace. Every detected span is swapped for a numbered placeholder such as
   <PERSON_1>, <EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>, <CREDIT_CARD_1>. The same real value maps to the same
   placeholder within a request, so the model can still reason about "the same person".
   The real-to-placeholder map is per-request and held in memory only.

3. Forward. Only the redacted text leaves the machine, to whichever provider you
   configured.

4. Restore. On the way back, the placeholders are rewritten to the original values in
   message content, in tool_calls[].function.arguments and the legacy
   function_call.arguments, and in reasoning traces (reasoning_content / reasoning).
   Restoration works for both non-streaming and streaming responses, including
   placeholders split across streamed deltas.

PrivAiTe scans places most flat-text scrubbers skip: tool-call arguments (parsed as
JSON and scrubbed value by value, including numeric leaves with at least 7 digits, so
a card number sent as a bare JSON number is caught) and multimodal content (text parts
of a content list are scrubbed; images and audio pass through untouched). This is why
it matters for agentic and multimodal traffic.

## Anonymization methods

Configured under pii.anonymization.method:

- placeholder (default): <PERSON_1>, <EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>. Reversible, restored in
  responses.
- fake_replacement: realistic fakes via Faker (Jean becomes Michel). Reversible.
- redact: [PERSON], [EMAIL_ADDRESS]. Irreversible, never restored.
- mask: ********. Irreversible, never restored.

redact and mask are lossy on purpose: the original never enters the reversible map, so
nothing is restored for those types and two values that mask to the same string can
never cross-restore. Per-entity overrides are supported, for example mask credit cards
and redact secrets while placeholdering everything else.

## Install and quickstart

From PyPI:

    pip install privaite

Then run the proxy and point any OpenAI-compatible client at http://localhost:8400/v1
using your proxy API key.

With Docker (image pre-downloads the ONNX model so it starts fast and works offline):

    docker compose up -d

From source (development):

    pip install -e .
    python -m spacy download en_core_web_lg
    python -m spacy download fr_core_news_md
    python -m privaite               # add --reload for auto-reload in dev

Any OpenAI-compatible client works without code changes. For Open WebUI (Docker), set
the OpenAI API connection URL to http://host.docker.internal:8400/v1 and the key to
your PRIVAITE_API_KEYS value. Any LiteLLM-supported provider can be configured as a
backend (openai/gpt-4o, ollama/llama3.1, and so on).

## Presets

Set under pii.preset. onnx is the default and works out of the box because onnxruntime
and the tokenizer ship as core dependencies.

    Preset  What runs                     Span recall*  False positives  Latency  Secrets
    onnx    Presidio + Privacy Filter     84.5%         2 / 14           ~0.5s    yes  (default)
    light   Presidio only                 62.4%         3 / 14           ~60ms    no
    max     onnx + GLiNER                  higher OOD**  more             ~0.7s    yes  (opt-in)

*Span-level recall on the 120-document AI4Privacy benchmark. Strict token-level recall
is 80.6% for onnx and 57.9% for light. Latency is hardware-dependent.

**max adds GLiNER (urchade/gliner_multi_pii-v1), a PII model trained on data
independent of AI4Privacy. On an out-of-distribution corpus it raises recall from about
84% to about 89% where the default already generalizes well, at the cost of more false
positives and a torch dependency. It needs pip install 'privaite[gliner]'; with max
selected but the package absent, the proxy fails to start with an install hint rather
than running with detection silently reduced. onnx stays the default.

Guidance: use onnx (default) for maximum coverage including secrets, passwords, API
keys, account numbers, and unusual names, accepting occasional false positives on
technical identifiers. Use light for the fastest path with near-zero false positives
when you only care about classic PII (names, emails, phones, cards, IBANs). Do not pin
detectors.presidio.entities to a short allowlist on the light path: it restricts
detection to only those types and roughly halves recall, and the proxy logs a startup
warning if it detects that configuration. Two further presets (standard, full) add BERT
NER and pull in PyTorch but do not improve much over spaCy.

## Endpoints

OpenAI-compatible HTTP API on port 8400:

- POST /v1/chat/completions : chat, streaming and non-streaming.
- POST /v1/completions      : text completions, streaming and non-streaming.
- POST /v1/embeddings       : embeddings (input is anonymized; embeddings are not
  de-anonymized).
- POST /v1/pii/inspect      : dry-run inspection (off by default). Returns the
  detections and anonymized preview for a submitted text and forwards nothing to any
  provider. New in 0.2.13.
- GET  /v1/models           : list configured models.
- GET  /health, GET /ready  : health and readiness checks.
- GET  /stats               : PII detection counts per session (never stores values;
  the session id is stored as a salted hash).

## Verify what gets redacted

Do not trust the proxy blindly. Two built-in, fully local ways to check on your own
data:

1. See exactly what the provider receives. Set:

       pii:
         deanonymization:
           enabled: false

   The response comes back without the real values restored, so what you read is
   literally what left for the provider (<PERSON_1>, <EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>, ...). Diff it
   against your input: every placeholder is a catch, every real value still visible is
   a miss. Works for tool-call arguments and streaming too.

2. Dry-run inspection endpoint. Enable it explicitly (off by default):

       pii:
         inspect:
           enabled: true

   Then submit text and get the detections back. Nothing is forwarded to any provider,
   nothing is logged, nothing is counted in /stats, and no mapping outlives the
   request:

       curl -s localhost:8400/v1/pii/inspect -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"text": "Contact Marie Dupont at marie@acme.com"}'

   The response lists each entity (type, exact span, score, source detector, and its
   replacement), an "anonymized" field that is the exact string the provider would have
   seen, and "would_block", the types your block_entities policy would reject.

## Configuration highlights

- block_entities (hard policy gate): list PII types that must never leave your network
  even as a placeholder. A request containing any listed type is rejected with HTTP 400
  and nothing is forwarded; the error names the type(s), never the value. Empty by
  default. Enforced at the single anonymization choke point, so it covers message
  content, multimodal text, and tool-call arguments alike.
- on_error: block (default). Anonymization fails closed: on an internal detector error
  the request is blocked, never forwarded with raw PII.
- Languages: seven supported through spaCy NER and contextual patterns. FR, EN, DE, ES,
  IT are benchmarked; PT and NL are best-effort. Each language needs its spaCy model.
- custom_patterns: add your own regex PII patterns (for example a CUSTOMER_ID or
  REFERENCE format) in YAML without touching code.
- passthrough.system_messages and passthrough.tool_calls skip the engine for those
  parts (and therefore skip block_entities). Both false by default.

## Integrations

If you do not want to run a separate proxy, PrivAiTe's engine runs in-process inside
two popular tools.

Open WebUI filter (integrations/openwebui/privaite_filter.py, v0.1.6). An Open WebUI
Filter Function: Admin Panel, Functions, "+", paste the file, save, enable, then open
its valves to pick the preset and languages. It anonymizes the outgoing request and
restores PII in the reply, covering message text, tool-call arguments, and multimodal
text. Requires privaite>=0.2.12. Also published on the Open WebUI community hub:
https://openwebui.com/posts/privaite_pii_anonymizer_351aa088

LiteLLM guardrail (integrations/litellm/privaite_guardrail.py). A LiteLLM custom
guardrail: mount it next to your config.yaml and reference it by dot-notation
(privaite_guardrail.PrivaiteGuardrail) with mode [pre_call, post_call]. It anonymizes
requests and restores responses inline, including inside tool-call arguments and the
legacy function_call, which LiteLLM's built-in Presidio guardrail does not cover. Chat
streaming restore is included. Requires privaite>=0.2.12.

Both integrations honor block_entities and fail closed if the installed privaite is too
old to enforce the gate, rather than silently forwarding PII.

## Benchmark (honest summary)

Measured on 120 real documents from the open AI4Privacy pii-masking-200k dataset on
Hugging Face (458 PII items across DE, EN, FR, IT, labeled by independent auditor
agents and cross-checked against the dataset's own sensitive mask), plus 14 clean
documents for false positives. The competitor rows are the real integrations at their
genuine best, not a strawman.

    Solution                       Recall (span)  Recall (strict)  False positives  Tool-call protection
    PrivAiTe onnx (default)        84.5%          80.6%            2 / 14           100%
    PrivAiTe light (full Presidio) 62.4%          57.9%            3 / 14           100%
    LiteLLM Presidio guardrail     70.3%          65.3%            3 / 14           0.6%
    LLM Guard (Anonymize)          76.9%          74.9%            5 / 14           0.6%

Span recall credits a multi-token span as caught when its exact full string disappears;
strict recall requires every token removed. On tool-call arguments, PrivAiTe removes
everything it detects (100% protection, 15.5% leak) while the others do not parse
tool-call JSON, so about 99% of the same PII survives inside a tool-call argument
(0.6% protection, 99.1% leak).

Two honesty notes, both favoring caution. LLM Guard's detection model is fine-tuned on
the exact dataset family behind this corpus, so its recall here is optimistic;
PrivAiTe's default model is not (OpenAI's model card states it did not train on it). An
out-of-distribution cross-check on a non-AI4Privacy corpus confirms this: the PrivAiTe
onnx stack holds about 84% recall while the AI4Privacy-tuned model drops to about 62%.

Full tables, competitor configs, methodology, and reproduction:
https://github.com/crp4222/privaite-bench
Out-of-distribution detail:
https://github.com/crp4222/privaite-bench/blob/main/OOD_COMPARISON.md
Head-to-head feature comparison:
https://github.com/crp4222/PrivAiTe/blob/main/docs/comparison.md

## Limitations (read before relying on it)

- Pseudonymization, not anonymization. The real-to-placeholder mapping is reversible by
  design (that is how responses are restored). Treat this as pseudonymization plus
  transfer minimization, not guaranteed anonymization and not a GDPR or HIPAA compliance
  guarantee. You remain the data controller. For irreversible removal use method redact
  or mask.
- Detection is best-effort. It is statistical and never 100%. A name the detector does
  not recognize reaches the provider. onnx has the best recall; treat the output as
  best-effort.
- Re-identification from context. Even with names replaced, surrounding text can stay
  identifying ("the CEO of <ORG_1> who resigned in March").
- Not scanned by default: messages[].name, top-level user and metadata, tools and
  functions definitions, JSON object keys inside tool arguments (renaming them would
  break the tool schema), and tokenized integer-array inputs. Keep PII out of those
  fields or strip them upstream. Set pii.strict: true to reject uninspectable content
  with a 400 instead of forwarding it.
- Informal dates ("last Tuesday", "il y a deux ans") are not detected. On the light
  (Presidio-only) preset, addresses, URLs, secrets, and passwords are not detected;
  those need the onnx preset.
- Not a defense against a compromised local machine (the mapping and raw text live in
  local memory) or against the provider correlating requests within a session.
